title: Indonesia’s tightening state grip on the economy
gist: Under President Prabowo Subianto, Indonesia is pursuing muscular, centralised economic nationalism — a one-million-hectare Merauke rice project, centralised commodity-export control, free nutritious meals and state cooperatives — but the article documents lagging delivery, military/police entanglement and echoes of Suharto-era patronage.

insights.claim: Prabowo's 2027 budget is built on 6% growth while keeping the deficit at 2.4% of GDP, below Indonesia's 3% legal ceiling, with food self-sufficiency near its centre.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: A 6% growth assumption against a capped deficit sets the fiscal frame investors should stress-test against lagging program delivery.
insights.quote: a 2027 budget built on 6% growth while keeping the deficit at 2.4% of GDP, below Indonesia’s 3% legal ceiling

insights.claim: The Merauke National Strategic Project combines one million hectares of new rice fields with large sugarcane and bioethanol developments, using its designation to accelerate permits and land acquisition over Indigenous consent objections.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: A vast fast-tracked agribusiness build with contested land rights carries execution, ESG and social-license risk for anyone exposed to Indonesian agri/bioethanol.

insights.claim: The wider Merauke development could convert nearly three million hectares of forest and swampland, and Indonesia already lost 433,751 hectares of forest in 2025 — up 66%.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: A 66% jump in forest loss ties Indonesia's food-security drive to deforestation exposure relevant to EU deforestation rules and carbon markets.
insights.quote: Indonesia already lost 433,751 hectares of forest in 2025, up 66%

insights.claim: The author argues the food-security justification for Merauke depends on uncertain yields and a remarkably low valuation of the land being cleared.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: A weak economic case flags the project as more political than commercially sound — a delivery-risk marker.
insights.quote: that case depends on uncertain yields and a remarkably low valuation of the land being cleared
insights.locator: Food security gives the project its economic justification

insights.claim: From January 2027 Indonesia's strategic commodity exports are expected to pass through a centralised state-controlled system meant to strengthen pricing power and curb under-invoicing, which Prabowo says may have cost the country US$5 billion.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: Centralised export routing changes how commodity rents and pricing power are captured — material for Indonesian coal, nickel and palm-oil trade flows.
insights.quote: which Prabowo says may have cost the country US$5 billion
insights.locator: Resource exports are also being pulled towards the centre

insights.claim: New state-owned intermediary PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia, under Danantara Indonesia, examined 6,500 export transactions worth US$14 billion in its first two months to review for discrepancies.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: A new state gatekeeper vetting $14bn of exports concentrates control over who captures commodity rents — watch Danantara's expanding remit.
insights.quote: it examined 6,500 transactions worth US$14 billion

insights.claim: By late July over 20,000 Nutrition Fulfilment Service Units were distributing meals under the National Nutrition Agency, with police reporting 828 operating kitchens (targeting 1,500 by year-end) and the military 113 operating plus 339 launched.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: Heavy military/police involvement in a flagship welfare program signals security-apparatus entrenchment in the civilian economy.
insights.locator: The same governing instinct reaches much closer

insights.claim: Indonesia Corruption Watch identified at least 102 MBG partner foundations linked to political and state power, including six with military affiliations, and some kitchens use land provided by military commands.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: Patronage links in program contracting echo New Order dynamics — a governance red flag for the program's integrity.
insights.quote: at least 102 MBG partner foundations linked to political and state power
insights.locator: The formal count understates their footprint

insights.claim: The MBG program still equals 45% of Indonesia's Rp508.2 trillion (US$28.5 billion) social-protection allocation and about 30% of education spending, even after its 2026 allocation was cut from Rp335 trillion to Rp229 trillion (US$12.8 billion).
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: One program consuming ~45% of social protection crowds out other spending — a fiscal-allocation distortion worth tracking.
insights.quote: it still equals 45% of Indonesia’s Rp508.2 trillion (US$28.5 billion) social-protection allocation

insights.claim: Much MBG spending targets school-age children beyond the first 1,000 days when nutrition most affects stunting (around 20% of under-fives), with only 275 kitchens across Papua's six provinces versus a 2,500 target, and at least 33,000 children hit by food poisoning by April.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: Mis-targeted spending plus food-safety failures mean the program buys visibility more than health outcomes — a delivery-quality warning.
insights.quote: at least 33,000 children had been affected by food poisoning
insights.locator: The latest official estimate puts stunting

insights.claim: Around 80,000 'Red and White' village cooperatives have been legally established but only 1,061 were operating by June 2026, with the Finance Ministry placing Rp200 trillion (US$12.2 billion) in state banks to expand lending.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: A gulf between 80,000 registered and 1,061 operating cooperatives, backed by $12bn of state-bank lending, signals large capital deployed ahead of real demand.
insights.quote: Around 80,000 cooperatives have been legally established, although only 1,061 were operating by June 2026
insights.locator: That appetite for visible scale continues

insights.claim: Some cooperatives have appeared in hard-to-reach locations including rice fields and beside cemeteries, suggesting the program was built around available land rather than actual demand, with state banks potentially financing the difference.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: Land-driven rather than demand-driven rollout raises non-performing-loan risk for state banks funding the scheme.
insights.quote: including rice fields and beside cemeteries

insights.claim: The author warns that without institutional discipline, accountability and willingness to abandon failure, Indonesia risks reversing post-Reformasi gains and reviving Suharto-era entanglement of centralised authority with patronage and politically connected business.
insights.speaker: Dyah (Prita) Pritadrajati
insights.so_what: The historical New Order parallel frames the central risk: economic nationalism sliding into patronage that burdens taxpayers and an insecure middle class.
insights.quote: state direction works only with institutional discipline, accountability, and a willingness to abandon failure
insights.locator: Indonesia still carries a strong memory of the New Order
